name: Nebushazban
title: Babylonian court official under Nebuchadnezzar
summary: Nebushazban was a high-ranking Babylonian official who served under King Nebuchadnezzar II. He is mentioned in connection with the conquest of Jerusalem in 586 BC, where he was among the Babylonian officers tasked with caring for the prophet Jeremiah. His title 'Rab-saris' indicates that he held a prominent position at the Babylonian court.

keyEvents.title: The Fall of Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Nebushazban was among the Babylonian officers who entered Jerusalem after a long siege. The Babylonian forces broke through the city walls and took position at the Middle Gate.

keyEvents.title: Order to Protect Jeremiah
keyEvents.description: Nebuchadnezzar gave orders to Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, to care for the prophet Jeremiah. Nebushazban was among the officers involved in carrying out this order.

keyEvents.title: Jeremiah Released from Captivity
keyEvents.description: Nebushazban was among those who sent word to bring Jeremiah from the guard court and handed him over to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, so that he could be taken home to live among the people.

keyEvents.title: The Babylonian Officers at the Middle Gate
keyEvents.description: After the city walls were breached, Nebuzaradan and the other Babylonian officers sat down at the Middle Gate as a sign of their control over the city.
